Person_A: What got me thinking about this was realizing that there is no reason to believe that consciousness automatically comes together with the ability to affect the surrounding environment in a way that communicates your consciousness. In evolved creatures, it seems to be the case that our consciousness arose out of an object that already had ways of interacting with its surroundings. But if it is possible for consciousness to arise in any kind of manufactured setting, then there is no reason to believe it could do anything other than simply experience some kind of awareness. The ability to connect that awareness with coordinated action is likely an artifact of our evolutionary past and not a characteristic of conscious experience.

I think this generally implies that it is actually likely that if some kind of "neural net" or web of connections similar to a brain had a light of awareness emerge within it, that we would have no way of ever confirming or even knowing it had happened. It would much more likely be a passive experience that was completely isolated from any means for communicating its awareness. I think most people, myself included, assumed that if the internet woke up, we'd suddenly see it manipulating websites or something like that. I now see no reason to believe that.
Person_B: Given "consciousness" is the function of "awareness", can awareness *of* some inputs exist without the function producing outputs?

Although it feels like this is so from introspection (e.g. I just sit here being aware without apparently "doing" anything), I doubt this is the case. There is a sense in which the function of awareness is in *some part* also the cause of *how* it sees those inputs e.g. whether it looks at a small group of inputs of large groups of inputs, a tree or a forest - so it must be producing output as well during the moment of being aware, perhaps outputs that are like an overlay on the original inputs.

Edit: So I contend awareness of something is not possible to exist passively as a receiver. Even a tuning fork being struck has outputs such as vibrating, which can be observed and measured.
